items.text: Swapping two rows changes the determinant's sign.
Scaling one row by c scales the determinant by c.
Adding a multiple of another row leaves the determinant unchanged.
Determinants apply to square matrices over a commutative field.
A triangular matrix has determinant equal to the product of its diagonal entries.
Cofactor expansion may use any fixed row r or fixed column c, but its signs alternate according to (-1)^(i+j).
The determinant is not the product of all matrix entries.
When elimination uses a row swap or row scaling, account for its effect before reading the diagonal product.
